This module runs automated data-quality checks (outliers, miscoded missing values, empty and constant columns, SPSS filter variables, category casing, problematic column names, mixed text encodings, spreadsheet formatting) on the extracted data files.
We examined 22 columns across 7 data files.

Spreadsheet formatting such as colour, merged cells, and blank rows/columns is not preserved when data are read programmatically or exported to CSV. Store data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable, no colour-encoded meaning) so it is machine-readable.
No file could be screened for careless responding.

**What this does not cover.** Only 0 of 7 data files could be screened: the rest had no detectable multi-item scale block, or too few respondents. Even in a screened file, these checks only look at multi-item rating scales — the only place where a repeated or flat answer pattern is interpretable. Single questions, open text, demographics and any item outside a detected scale block are never examined. A respondent can therefore answer most of a survey carelessly and still not be flagged here, and finding nothing is not evidence that a dataset is free of careless responding.

-  We classified 12 files: 11 data, 1 unknown.
-  We found 11 tabular data files and extracted 22 columns from 7 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1).
-  The study-group step did not get an answer for 11 files (the model request failed); they were grouped by the fallback rules instead.
-  4 files read as a table but are not a usable rectangular dataset (readxl_type-me.xls: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; xl_bools.xlsx: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; xl_header_only.xlsx: the file has no data rows or columns; xl_title.xlsx: 100% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: readxl_type-me.xls, xl_bools.xlsx, xl_header_only.xlsx, xl_title.xlsx. We ran automated data-quality checks on 22 columns; 1 column has at least one potential issue (1 column with no observed values (entirely empty)). 6 of 12 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).
